editions.text:
The day's 26 species was the most of the eight days, matching October 25, and its 201 visits sat close to the week's average of 202.0. Tufted Titmouse led the visits with 64, followed by Carolina Wren with 32 and Carolina Chickadee with 24. Heard detections totaled 326, below the week's average of 378.4, with Eastern Towhee leading at 53.

Fourteen species were recorded on all seven days, this one included, among them Blue Jay, Northern Cardinal, Song Sparrow, and Tufted Titmouse. Eastern Screech-Owl was recorded on six of the seven days, including this one. Red-shouldered Hawk was recorded on each of the previous seven days but not today. Rose-breasted Grosbeak returned after 16 days away, last recorded on October 12.

The audio source changed many times through the day, so the heard total draws on more than one microphone. No species was seen or heard for the first time at this station. One highlight was a Blue Jay that perched on the water bowl's rim, bent to drink, and flew off.
